name: ES Spatial-or-Topological Opening Convexity v1
instrument: ES continuous front-month signal with one MES execution unit
hypothesis: An opening auction can leave exploitable convexity through either spatial compression or topological simplicity. A range below its recent median indicates limited spatial exploration; a center-crossing count below its recent median indicates unusually one-sided inventory formation. In either state, direction should be supplied by a later accepted opening-range escape rather than forecast in advance.

rules.spatial_state: opening high-low range is strictly below the shifted trailing 60-session median opening range
rules.auction_center: volume-weighted mean of one-minute typical price, where typical price is (high + low + close) / 3
rules.rotation_count: number of sign changes in one-minute closes relative to the completed opening auction center; exact-center observations inherit the nearest prior sign, with initial missing signs backfilled
rules.topological_state: rotation count is strictly below the shifted trailing 60-session median rotation count
rules.confirmation: beginning 10:00, scan non-overlapping five-minute bars and use the first close strictly outside the opening high or low
rules.entry: next one-minute open plus one adverse ES tick
rules.stop: opening-range midpoint plus one adverse ES tick
rules.same_bar_rule: a stop touched anywhere in a one-minute bar is filled at the frozen stop price
rules.survivor_exit: 15:30 open plus one adverse ES tick
rules.position_limit: one MES and at most one trade per RTH session

economics.slippage_model: one adverse tick at entry; one adverse tick at the time exit; stop itself is placed one adverse tick beyond the midpoint

validation_disclosure.reason: The spatial-compression component had already been evaluated on 2024-2025 as a prior candidate. The low-rotation topology component and the exact OR-union were frozen before their first 2024-2025 evaluation.
prohibited_actions: Do not tune the 60-session lookback after secondary holdout.
Do not replace strict less-than with inclusive less-than-or-equal after secondary holdout.
Do not select a side, year, state, or time subset after secondary holdout.

verdict: Rejected. The newly introduced topological-only state appeared stable across all development years and both directions but reversed severely in secondary holdout. Do not remove that state after observing the result, and do not promote the union. This is evidence that opening path topology is an unstable classifier despite an appealing mechanism.
